thread.title: Bears Claw Stocks Again; Will Apple Keep Its Uptrend Intact?

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Bears Claw Stocks Again; Will Apple Keep Its Uptrend Intact?
text:
Broad selling rocked U.S. stocks again in afternoon trading Thursday, but the market shaved some of its losses.
X Meanwhile, Apple ( AAPL ) outperformed on a relative basis, wiping away minor early losses and ticking up a few pennies at 159.58 in heavy turnover.
The megacap tech, currently showing a market value of $810 billion, continues to test institutional buying support at the 200-day moving average, a longer-term support level. A strong rally off the 200-day line would give only those investors with a really big profit cushion in the stock an opportunity to add some shares to the position.
However, with IBD's current market outlook , updated every day in The Big Picture column, at "Uptrend under pressure," all new buys carry higher-than-usual risk.
Plus, consider this: Apple has already given back all the gains from an Oct. 27 breakout past a second-stage cup with handle at 160.97. The gain from that breakout had reached nearly 12%.
At 2:15 p.m. ET, the   fell 2% after hitting a session low of 24,213, off 2.7%. At least half of the 30 Dow components dropped 2 points or more. The Dow transports skidded 2% lower.
A fall by the Dow industrials below this week's lowest price of 23,778 would put the blue chip index back into an intermediate-level correction, or equal to a minimum drop of 10% from its 52-week high.
The S&P 500 fell 1.6% while the Nasdaq composite sank more than 1.8%. The Nasdaq 100-tracking PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) dived back below its 50-day moving average with a 2.2% drop to 156.69. Earlier in the week, QQQ fell as much as 9.3% below its Jan. 26 all-time peak of 170.95. A drop of 10% or more from a 52-week peak would qualify as an intermediate-level correction.
The last time that happened for QQQ? From December 2015 to February 2016, when the ETF dropped almost 18% from a 52-week peak of 115.75.
Volume accelerated vs. the same time on Wednesday on both main exchanges.
Semiconductor equipment, computer networking, auto, game software and data storage firms still paced the overall decline, each sinking 3% or more. Oil drilling, trucking and RV stocks also slid hard. But beaten down fiber optic telecom gear, dairy, drug wholesale, tobacco and gold mining shares bucked the decline. The Dow utility average, already in an intermediate-level correction, was off just 0.1%.
Stocks resumed their harsh selling amid another decline in government bond prices.
The yield on the benchmark U.S. Treasury 10-year bond moved up to as high as 2.87%, edging closer to its January 2014 high of 3.04%.
Numerous tech leaders are testing the bulls at the 50-day moving average, including security software firm Proofpoint ( PFPT ), which on Tuesday reported a 61% jump in fourth-quarter earnings to 29 cents a share. Revenue grew 36% to $145.4 million, marking a quarterly record and stretching its streak of 30%-plus year-over-year increases in the top line to 17 quarters.
Electronic Arts ( ERTS ) still shows a large air cushion above its own 50-day line. The video game giant, down 3% to 119.89, is back below a 122.89 cup entry.
Alphabet ( GOOGL ), which slashed through its 50-day line on Monday, slumped another 2% to 1,034 and is now just 3% above a recent flat-base breakout point at 1,006.29.
Going back to Apple, the stock is trying to preserve a fine long-term uptrend that began with the formation of a long bottoming base throughout much of 2016. That base work culminated with the Jan. 6, 2017, breakout from a first-stage cup with handle at 118.12.
Amid that run-up, Apple had tested the medium-term 50-day moving average several times, but showed the strength to move higher. However, the daily chart shows multiple sell-offs in heavy volume over the past four weeks — 10 big down sessions in above-average trade, to be exact.
That's in contrast with seven up days in heavy turnover over the same period. Thus, the IBD Stock Checkup shows that Apple's Accumulation/Distribution Rating has fallen to a danger-level D- on a scale of A (heavy net buying by funds over the past 13 weeks) to E (heavy net selling).
